about: Facts authors went to the engine's source for. Each was measured or read when the engine was at the version above; ENGINE.md flags them when the engine's version differs.

facts.text: A glTF imports at 100 scene units per metre with a half turn about x, so its y grows downward; read the model's own bounds in the program to size it and to stand it on the ground (see examples/model_and_environment.py).
light@castShadow defaults to false: without one shadow-casting light no object is seen resting on anything. Set it on the key.
facts.source: SKILL.md trap rows; the kit's rule:shadow

facts.text: A dome light's environmentVisible defaults to false: the HDRI lights and reflects but the background is a black void until it is set true.

The path tracer finds an emissive surface only by chance, so an emissive object lights nothing reliably and shows as specks; light the scene with a light and let the emissive surface be seen, not relied on.
A metal's reflectance is its baseColor: a dark baseColor on a metal is a dark mirror, not a coloured finish.
A medium forces the path tracer at 4 samples and 2 bounces whatever the camera asks for; a document with a medium costs like a path-traced one and pathSamples does not buy quality there.
An HDRI is prefiltered for reflections at 512 px: a mirror-sharp reflection of an environment is limited by that, not by the file's resolution.
camera@shutterAngle is never read by either renderer; it is accepted by the schema and has no effect.
